sections.html: The 5 species of the genus Crossoloricaria all look very similar to the flounder-like loricariid genus Pseudohemiodon. These fish also have a flattened body and small eyes set far apart on a triangular head. The difference between the two genera is that Crossoloricaria lacks the ventral bony plates; only along the medial line of the underside is there a small row of tiny bony plates. C. cephalaspis does not grow larger than 20 cm.
This species originates from the north of Colombia.

They absolutely need a sandy substrate in which they can bury themselves as deep as possible. This means they are often difficult to spot at all. When newly introduced to the aquarium they only come out of the sand at night, but after a period of acclimatisation they appear at feeding time.
